record.paper_title: New results and open questions for SIR-PH epidemic models with linear birth rate, loss of immunity, vaccination, and disease and vaccination fatalities
record.context_brief: Global stability for the full ten-parameter SAIR/V+S model
record.original_question: Can global asymptotic stability be proved for the ten-parameter SAIR/V+S model with standard incidence, linear birth rate, susceptible S, exposed/asymptomatic E, infective I, recovered/vaccinated R, vaccination, loss of immunity, exposed and infective transmission, and disease-induced deaths, rather than being supported only by numerical simulations?

evidence.quote:
We generalize the uniqueness of the endemic point and the local stability results of these six papers,
and at the same time draw attention to certain unnecessary assumptions and mistakes. The hardest
issue, that of global stability, is only illustrated via some numerical simulations.

In this paper, we consider a ten parameters SAIR (also called SEIR in the classic literature [51])
epidemic model inspired by [24, 31, 34, 48, 10, 37, 16, 40], which we call SAIR/V+S (or SAIR
for short), since it groups together immunized people in an R/V compartment.

artifact.status_search_result: Global stability for the full ten-parameter SAIR/V+S model with standard incidence, vaccination, loss of immunity, and disease-induced deaths in both the E and I compartments does not appear to have been established in full generality. Related works prove global stability only under restrictive assumptions (e.g., no disease-induced deaths, equal removal rates, only one infectious compartment transmitting, or constraints linking the rates of loss of natural and vaccine immunity), and global stability for the full model is typically supported only by numerical simulations. No source establishing the general result was found.

status_evidence.title: Global stability of an SAIRS epidemic model with vaccinations, transient immunity and treatment
status_evidence.snippet: Global stability results are obtained for an SAIRS model with vaccinations under specific assumptions, not for the full ten-parameter model with disease-induced deaths in both E and I compartments.
status_evidence.claim: Global stability is proved only under restrictive parameter assumptions, not in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Global stability of SAIRS epidemic models
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes global asymptotic stability of the disease-free and endemic equilibria of SAIRS models under conditions on parameters; does not cover the full ten-parameter SAIR/V+S model with both asymptomatic and symptomatic disease-induced deaths.
status_evidence.claim: Existing global stability results require additional assumptions beyond the general ten-parameter setting.

status_evidence.title: An extended epidemic model with vaccination: Weak-immune SIRVI
status_evidence.snippet: Analyzes related SIRV-type models with vaccination and waning immunity, leaving global stability of more general models as an open issue often illustrated only numerically.
status_evidence.claim: Related literature supports that the general problem remains open and is typically addressed only numerically.
